proof_summary: For inputs above the thresholds, a positive count supplies primes giving the required Goldbach or Lemoine decomposition directly, while finite tables of explicit prime decompositions cover all smaller admissible inputs. If cousin-prime pairs were bounded by \(B\), applying the hypothesis to a sufficiently large even \(n\) would produce two such pairs based at \(q\) and \(p-6\), forcing \(n=q+(p-6)+6\le 2B+6\), a contradiction.
